questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Carnegie built a telegraph company from a single office
Carnegie's early messenger years, his raise, his family, and telegraphy
How Colonel Glass left the telegraph for a political career
The building of the Allegheny River bridge in Pittsburgh
questions.explain: Carnegie recounts his messenger work, his joyful pay raise, family life and learning the telegraph.

questions.q: How did the Carnegie family repay Mrs. Henderson's loan?
options: With a draft bought using two hundred half-dollars saved in a stocking
By selling the furniture the family had slowly bought
With a gift of money from Colonel Glass one Saturday
Through wages sent by an uncle working in Dunfermline
questions.explain: Mother saved silver half-dollars in a stocking until two hundred were gathered, then he obtained a draft to repay the twenty pounds.

questions.q: What new monthly wage did Mr. Glass give Carnegie?
options: Eleven and a quarter dollars
Fifteen dollars
Twenty dollars
Thirteen and a half dollars
questions.explain: Glass said Carnegie was worth more and would be paid thirteen and a half dollars a month.

questions.q: How did Carnegie first take a telegraph message?
options: He copied one as Mr. Brooks dictated it from the instrument
He answered a Philadelphia death-message call and asked for slow sending
He was assigned to a message when an operator fell ill
He read it from a printed slip handed over the counter
questions.explain: He answered the Pittsburgh call, took Philadelphia's death message at slow speed, and ran out with it.

questions.q: Why did the other boys think Carnegie was mean?
options: He refused to share his lunch with the other messenger boys
He was paid a higher wage than the others from the start
He did not spend his extra dimes because the family needed them
He reported the other boys to Colonel Glass for idling
questions.explain: The boys saw him not spending dimes but did not know he saved every penny for his family.
